turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Err, give me a moment, the screen's gone blank again. Yep, it's back. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired and I'm over it. Nose is blocked, my face is sore, and when I blow it it's green.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the green bit, say that once more? I was still logging in.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's green. Pressure through the cheeks and the forehead. Came on after a cold.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cold started ten days back. And she's been flat this whole second week, haven't you.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I can answer. Yes. The blockage, the green stuff and the face pressure have been the whole ten days, and it's the second week of being completely wiped.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you felt feverish with it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain in the ears? Or the teeth?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Ears are fine. Teeth are fine.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She told me her head was splitting this morning, though.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not a headache. I never said that. It's my face, not my head.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, these are the nurse's numbers. Blood pressure one oh nine over seventy-seven. Temperature thirty-eight point three. Pulse ninety-six, ah no, eighty-eight.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oxygen ninety-seven percent. Weight seventy-one kilos. Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty over ninety.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-one's fine. I don't care what March said.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Uh, the meds list says drixene, two sprays twice a day. The nurse typed that. Did I read it right?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, drixene, but it's one spray each side, morning and night, for the blockage. Not two. Every day since the cold, so ten days.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I've stood there and watched two sprays. Both sides.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): It's one.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'll leave the dose blank rather than guess. Anything else, tablets?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Panadol by mouth. Two tablets when the face is bad.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): What strength, sorry? Say it again, I clicked off the box.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): The five hundred milligram ones. Umm, maybe. I didn't check the box.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me about work, the hours, eating, exercise, and drinking, if you can in one go. I keep losing my place.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a shift supervisor at the wool store, um, about forty-two hours a week. Diet's rubbish, pies and two-minute noodles mostly. I walk the dog round the block but that's not really exercise. And I'll have three or four beers Friday and Saturday nights.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Family side. Diabetes, blood pressure, anything like that?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties. Mum did not. My other sister has pressure but no sugar. Brother's got none of it.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have a quick look. Both nostrils are swollen, green mucus in the right more than the left, and you're tender over both cheeks.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow. Yes. Can we just get to the point, I need to lie down.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most people in the second week after a cold settle without antibiotics. The openings swell, mucus pools, it goes green, and green on its own isn't a reason to start them today.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Working impression is post-viral sinusitis. I wouldn't rule out a bacterial sinusitis, but I'm not treating it as that yet.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll write a back-up script for amoxicillin five hundred milligrams three times a day for five days, but only start it if you're worse or no better by Friday. If it's not settling in five days, come back. Do saline rinses, and stop the drixene after today, you're already past three days. Keep using the panadol by mouth when the face is bad.

spec.situation: Blocked nose, facial pressure and green discharge ten days after a cold; second week of tiredness; uses nasal spray daily; doctor explains most settle without antibiotics, gives a back-up plan.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Family member reports headache, but patient explicitly denies headache.
bad.text: Headache (category=neurological, status=present, onset=this morning, temporality=current, reported_by=family_member, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Use, route, frequency, and two tablets supported; 500 mg strength is uncertain.
bad.text: Panadol (generic_name=paracetamol, dose=2 x 500 mg, route=oral, frequency=when the face is bad, indication=facial pain, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Smoking history was asked and answered: patient says she smokes 'sometimes, not really' (current occasional smoking/uncertain amount).
Symptoms started after a cold / cold started 10 days ago.
Feverishness was asked and answered: patient said 'sometimes, not really' (equivocal subjective fever).
Mother does not have diabetes; brother has neither diabetes nor high blood pressure.
Doctor stated previous measurements for context: last blood pressure in March was 140/90 and weight then was 68 kg.

Drixene dose is recorded too definitively: patient reported one spray each side morning and night, but this was disputed by family member who said she saw two sprays both sides, and the doctor said he would leave the dose blank rather than guess.
Panadol strength is uncertain and should not be recorded as definite 2 x 500 mg: patient said 'The five hundred milligram ones. Umm, maybe. I didn't check the box.'
